captions.text: Open Shifts and find the Calendar section.
Add Static Shift creates a dated coverage window for selected units.
Use this when you need a fixed commitment, such as a community standby, a security
detail or a search support period.
The calendar in this exercise is November.
Select Add Static Shift to open the form.
Use a separate training unit while you learn the save and update process.

scenes.title: Name the shift and choose a readable color

captions.text: Give the shift a recognizable Name.
The example uses Verified static coverage.
Choose a light Color so the calendar’s black text stays readable; the help
beside the field calls this out.
Add a Description explaining the work and any coordination instructions.
This fictional description also reminds the editor to verify dates
and retained units before updating.
A clear title and description help people recognize the commitment
when they open it from the calendar.

scenes.title: Set the local window and select the unit

captions.text: Set Start Date and Time to November twelfth at nine in the morning, and End
Date and Time to five that afternoon.
The start help describes when entities are committed; the end help describes
when they are available again.
Under Units, select the fictional static demo unit and confirm its selected tag.
Check both dates and the chosen unit before Create Static Shift.
Dismiss the date picker so it does not cover the unit selection or save control.

scenes.title: Save and verify the actual day detail

captions.text: Select Create Static Shift, then open the matching event from the calendar.
View Static Shift Day shows November twelfth at nine, the shift title and
description, and the selected unit.
This is the saved result, not the preparation form.
The training unit has no configured unit-role slots, so this example does not
claim that any person has been assigned.
Compare the saved day and unit with the intended commitment before moving on.
Select Edit Static Shift.
The reopened dates retain nine in the morning through five in the afternoon.
Read the yellow warning before Update: editing clears the shift’s
assignments or signups and rebuilds them from the new settings.
In this version, the Units selection is initially empty on Edit.
Deliberately select every unit you intend to retain.
Coordinate the change before updating a staffed operational
shift; do not assume a saved date change preserves existing signups.

scenes.title: Change the window and retain the unit

captions.text: For this disposable exercise, move the window to November thirteenth, ten in
the morning through six in the evening.
Reselect the same training unit and verify its tag.
Review the warning and select Update once.
Open the saved calendar event again.
Its day detail now shows November thirteenth at ten,
with the same unit still listed.
That readback checks both the new date and the unit submitted with the update.

scenes.title: Reopen once more and leave safely

captions.text: Reopen Edit to check the persisted start and end values: ten A M and
six P M on November thirteenth.
The Units picker is empty again in this editor, even though the saved
day detail just showed the unit.
Do not submit another update while merely reviewing.
Select Cancel to leave the stored shift unchanged.
Use the saved day detail to verify the current unit commitment, and
review the edit warning whenever a change is actually required.

scenes.title: Apply fixed coverage across department types

captions.text: Use this same create, verify and carefully update process for search and rescue,
security companies, wildland contractors and industrial emergency teams.
Community paramedicine, mental health response, fire and E M S teams can
plan fixed support windows as well.
Choose a meaningful unit and coverage period, keep calendar
labels readable, and verify the saved result after every change.
This lesson covers a fixed unit commitment; recurring rotations
and personnel signup workflows have their own walkthroughs.
